### Project Name

Open Responses

### Project Description

Open Responses is a vendor-neutral specification and conformance project for language-model APIs, derived from the OpenAI Responses API. It gives model providers, inference gateways, client libraries, and agent frameworks a common representation for requests, output items, multimodal content, tool calls, and streaming events. Implementers can preserve these semantics across providers while retaining clearly defined extension points.

The public project launched in January 2026. It includes the specification, machine-readable OpenAPI schemas, dated specification revisions, documentation, and browser-based and command-line acceptance tests. Subsequent revisions have expanded the protocol, including WebSocket transport and compaction support.

### Alignment with AAIF Mission

Open Responses contributes a shared model-inference contract to the open agentic stack. Consistent messages, tool calls, item lifecycles, and streaming behavior reduce provider-specific integration work and make agents, gateways, and SDKs more portable. The public specification, acceptance tests, multi-vendor participation, and open technical governance provide a practical basis for interoperability and long-term compatibility. Neutral foundation stewardship would help more implementers evolve and test that contract together.

### Relation to Existing AAIF Projects

Open Responses complements AAIF's existing projects at the model-inference layer:

- MCP connects agents to tools, data, and external capabilities; Open Responses defines the client/provider exchange that requests model output and represents tool use.
- AGENTS.md supplies repository-local instructions; Open Responses supplies the structured runtime interface to a model provider.
- goose is an agent implementation that can use interoperable provider interfaces.
- agentgateway provides routing, policy, and observability for agent traffic; Open Responses supplies a common inference contract that gateways can expose or route.
- A2A supports communication and delegation between agents; Open Responses addresses an agent's interaction with its underlying model provider.

### Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption

Typical uses include exposing one model API across providers, preserving tool-call and streaming semantics in inference gateways, building portable agent clients, and running acceptance tests against provider implementations.

Independently operated hosted services provide concrete public adoption evidence:
- OpenAI's Responses API, the inspiration for the project, is the default API fro all modern models.
- Vercel AI Gateway exposes the OpenResponses endpoint at https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/responses. 
- Databricks Model Serving exposes /serving-endpoints/open-responses for multiple foundation-model providers. 
- Amazon Bedrock Responses API
- Microsoft Responses API
- Ramp Router API

### License

Apache-2.0 for code; CC-BY-4.0 for specification text and documentation, per the technical charter.

### Governance Model

The public technical charter establishes contributors, maintainers, core maintainers, a lead core maintainer, and a technical steering committee (TSC). Governance seats belong to individuals; a single vendor may not hold a majority of core-maintainer seats. Technical work proceeds through public discussion and consensus. When a vote is necessary, each TSC member has one vote, quorum is 50%, ordinary meeting decisions require a majority of those present, and electronic votes require a majority of the full TSC. Charter changes require two-thirds of the full TSC. The lead core maintainer resolves technical deadlocks under the charter.

Technical charter: https://www.openresponses.org/governance
Contribution process and current roster: https://github.com/openresponses/openresponses/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING

### CI/CD & Release Workflow

The public repository uses GitHub Actions for pull-request acceptance checks. The workflow installs dependencies from the frozen Bun lockfile and runs formatting checks, Bun tests, and Python unit tests. Implementers can also run the same conformance suite through the documentation website or the CLI.

The release process regenerates the canonical OpenAPI schema, creates immutable date-versioned OpenAPI and prose snapshots, updates the generated specification/reference pages, and records changes in CHANGELOG.md. Published specification revisions include 2026-01-15 and 2026-04-24. Releases are change-driven; a fixed release cadence or LTS commitment is not currently claimed. The default branch is main.

PR workflow: https://github.com/openresponses/openresponses/blob/main/.github/workflows/pr-acceptance.yml
Release procedure: https://github.com/openresponses/openresponses/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING
Release history: https://www.openresponses.org/changelog
Acceptance tests: https://www.openresponses.org/compliance

### Public-Facing Contribution Process for Specifications

Contributors propose changes through public GitHub issues and pull requests. Changes affecting the specification, compatibility, or conformance should begin with a proposal that explains the problem, proposed API/specification shape, compatibility implications, any implementation or migration work, and a test plan. After discussion, the implementation PR should include the corresponding specification, documentation, and tests. The project seeks consensus and uses the TSC process in its technical charter when a decision needs escalation. Code contributions require a DCO sign-off.

### Publicly Accessible Issue Tracker

https://github.com/openresponses/openresponses/issues

### External Project Dependencies

The specification is implementation-neutral. The documentation, schema-generation, and acceptance-test tooling uses the following direct dependencies, grouped by their publisher-declared licenses:

- MIT: @astrojs/mdx, @astrojs/react, @tailwindcss/typography, @tailwindcss/vite, @types/bun, @types/react, @types/react-dom, astro, astro-expressive-code, astro-mermaid, mermaid, oas, react, react-dom, zod, @kubb/cli, @kubb/core, @kubb/plugin-oas, @kubb/plugin-zod, @typespec/prettier-plugin-typespec, autoprefixer, concurrently, husky, lint-staged, postcss, prettier, prettier-plugin-astro, prettier-plugin-tailwindcss, tailwindcss, and Python pyrailroad.
- Apache-2.0: TypeScript and the OpenAI Python SDK.
- MPL-2.0: @vercel/analytics.
- CC0-1.0: railroad-diagrams.

### Leadership Team & Decision Process

The technical steering committee consists of Steve Coffey (OpenAI, lead core maintainer), Ankit Mathur (Databricks), Anthony Liguori (Amazon), Ben Burtenshaw (Hugging Face), Devon Rifkin (Ollama), Ji Huang (OpenAI), Matt Apperson (OpenRouter), and Shaun Smith (Hugging Face). The current roster is maintained at https://github.com/openresponses/openresponses/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING#maintainers.

The TSC owns technical direction, specification changes, compatibility/versioning policy, reference implementations, and conformance tooling. Proposals and decisions are public. The project seeks consensus, uses the charter's voting rules when necessary, and provides a lead-maintainer tie-break process for unresolved technical disputes. Promotion, removal, leadership succession, and charter-amendment procedures are documented at https://www.openresponses.org/governance.


### Roadmap

Current public work is tracked in GitHub issues and specification revisions:

- Provider capability matrix: https://github.com/openresponses/openresponses/issues/80

- OAuth: https://github.com/openresponses/openresponses/issues/64
- Tool-approval semantics: https://github.com/openresponses/openresponses/issues/62
- Stream recovery: https://github.com/openresponses/openresponses/issues/14

Specification history: https://www.openresponses.org/changelog

### Security

Current public practices include pull-request review, automated formatting and unit tests, locked dependency installation, DCO sign-off for code contributions, and provider conformance tests. These support contribution provenance and compatibility, but are not a substitute for vulnerability management or a security audit.

Security page: https://github.com/openresponses/openresponses/security

### Infrastructure Needs or Requests

Potential foundation support includes neutral stewardship of the project domain, GitHub organization, and other project accounts; CI capacity for specification generation and acceptance tests; release/signing infrastructure as versioned packages or compatibility badges are introduced; and community support for issue triage, contribution review, and implementer coordination. Any asset transfers or associated commitments would be finalized through the contribution agreement.


### Additional Information

We request Impact-stage consideration for Open Responses. The project brings a public specification, acceptance tooling, multi-vendor technical governance, and independently documented hosted implementations.
